bibliography.note: Jamie D. Chippett, MSc thesis, Department of Biology, Memorial University of Newfoundland, March 2004; title matches. The ledger's '(Cited via COSEWIC 2014)' can go: the thesis itself has now been read, and every use below can cite it directly

claims.claim: the only banded killifish count found is from the shallows of two Newfoundland ponds (about 20,600 fish in August; Chippett 2004, via COSEWIC 2014)
claims.location: p. 77 (PDF p. 90), ch. 5; p. 22 (PDF p. 35), ch. 2; methods p. 17 (PDF p. 30)
claims.quote: the August estimate was for 20,569 individuals (95% confidence limits 12,529-40,201)
claims.conditions: Schnabel mark–recapture with anal-fin clips over a week each in July and August 1999, Indian Bay watershed; July 1,209 (95 % CL 619–3,423) when the water was cooler; ch. 2 labels the estimate '(Third Pond)', while the population occupies the adjoining waters of Backup and Third Ponds (Fig. 2-5, p. 23; p. 27); the thesis gives no habitat area, so no density
claims.note: 'two ponds' fits the population's range (Backup and Third Ponds); the thesis itself names Third Pond for the estimate. Cite Chippett 2004 directly

claims.claim: banded killifish spawn at 19–23 °C in Newfoundland
claims.quote: late June through to the middle of August when water temperatures reached between 19-23°C
claims.conditions: spawning behaviour observed in the Indian Bay watershed, Newfoundland
claims.note: the next page (p. 74, ch. 5.4.3) says spawning 'was observed at water temperatures of 22-24°C in the shallows' — the thesis is not fully consistent; 19–23 °C is its main statement

claims.conditions: 2.2 mm = mean diameter of eggs taken from Indian Bay females in late July (ovarian eggs); 2.0 mm is Cooper's (1936) mainland value, which Chippett relays; large females held up to 420 eggs (vs 250, Carlander 1969)

claims.claim: eggs on adhesive threads, mostly on Potamogeton
claims.quote: most often in association with pondweed species of the genus
claims.conditions: spawning behaviour 'most often in association with pondweed species of the genus Potamogeton' (near P. epihydrus, p. 25); the adhesive threads are from Richardson (1939), relayed: 'females release eggs with individual adhesive threads that adhere to aquatic vegetation'
claims.note: strictly, Chippett saw spawning at Potamogeton rather than eggs on it; 'spawns mostly at Potamogeton' is the exact reading

claims.paper: Table 3.6-1 (banded killifish, 'none' in the care column)
claims.note: the thesis does not discuss parental care (searched 'parental', 'guard', 'care'); the research notes take 'no parental care' from COSEWIC 2014's summary — credit COSEWIC (or another source) for it, not Chippett

notes: The thesis, earlier blocked for size, is now on disk. The paper's numbers check against it; drop 'via COSEWIC 2014' throughout and re-credit the 'no parental care' cell. Other useful values: fyke nets caught no killifish below 12 °C, with much larger catches at higher temperatures (Fig. 2-4, p. 21); occupied areas shallow, mud substrate, dense vegetation (Table 2-2, Fig. 2-5); quadrat plants at 4–16 per 0.25 m², dominated by Lobelia dortmanna (p. 70); Indian Bay fish ate a high share of chironomid larvae (p. 76); the Newfoundland area of occurrence is < 200 km² (p. 83).
